Affenpinscher.text: The Affenpinscher is a German breed of small toy dog of Pinscher type.

Afghan Hound.text: The Afghan Hound is a hound distinguished by its thick, fine, silky coat, and a tail with a ring curl at the end. The breed originates in the cold mountains of Afghanistan.

Airedale Terrier.text: The Airedale Terrier, also called Bingley Terrier and Waterside Terrier, is a dog breed of the terrier type that originated in the valley (dale) of the River Aire, in the West Riding of Yorkshire, England.

Akita (dog breed).text: The Akita Inu  is a Japanese dog breed of large size. Originating from the mountains of northern Japan, the Akita has a short double coat similar to that of many other northern spitz breeds.

Alaskan Klee Kai.text: The Alaskan Klee Kai is an American spitz-type breed of dog, developed in the late 20th century as a companion-sized dog resembling the larger Alaskan Malamute and Siberian Husky.

Alaskan Malamute.text: The Alaskan Malamute is a large spitz-type breed of dog that was originally bred for its strength and endurance to haul heavy freight as a sled dog.

American Bull Dog.text: The American Bulldog is a large, muscular breed of mastiff-type dog. Their ancestors were brought to the British North American colonies where they worked on small farms and ranches.

American Bully.text: The American Bully is a modern breed of dog that was developed as a companion dog, and originally standardized and recognized as a breed in 2004 by the American Bully Kennel Club (ABKC).

American Cocker Spaniel.text: The American Cocker Spaniel is a breed of sporting dog.

American English Coonhound.text: The American English Coonhound, also referred to as the English Coonhound or the Redtick Coonhound, is a breed of coonhound that originated in and is typically bred in the Southern United States.

American Eskimo Dog.text: The American Eskimo Dog is a breed of companion dog, originating in Germany. The American Eskimo Dog is a member of the Spitz family.

American Eskimo dog.text: The American Eskimo Dog is a breed of companion dog, originating in Germany. The American Eskimo Dog is a member of the Spitz family.

American Foxhound.text: The American Foxhound is a breed of dog, closely related to the English Foxhound. They are scent hounds, bred to hunt foxes by scent.

American Hairless Terrier.text: The American Hairless Terrier is a breed of companion dog from the United States that was developed from naturally hairless Rat Terriers.

American Leopard Hound.text: The American Leopard Hound is an American breed of hunting dog. It is recognized by the United Kennel Club (UKC) as a scenthound and is in the American Kennel Club's Foundation Stock Service.

American Staffordshire Terrier.text: The American Staffordshire Terrier, also known as the AmStaff, is a medium-sized, short-coated American dog breed recognized by the American Kennel Club, but not the United Kennel Club, which instead allows American Staffordshire Terriers to be registered under the American Pit Bull Terrier breed.

American Water Spaniel.text: The American Water Spaniel is a breed of spaniel which originated in the United States.

Anatolian Shepherd Dog.text: The Kangal Shepherd Dog or Turkish Kangal is a traditional Turkish breed of large livestock guardian dog.

Australian Cattle Dog.text: The Australian Cattle Dog, or simply Cattle Dog, is a breed of herding dog developed in Australia for droving cattle over long distances across rough terrain.

Australian Kelpie.text: The Australian Kelpie, or simply Kelpie, is an Australian sheepdog capable of mustering and droving with little or no guidance. It is a medium-sized dog and comes in a variety of colours.

Australian Shepherd.text: The Australian Shepherd, also known as the Aussie, is a breed of herding dog from the United States. Despite the name, the breed was developed in California in the 19th century.

Australian Silky Terrier.text: The Australian Silky Terrier or simply Silky Terrier is a small breed of dog of the terrier dog type.

Australian Terrier.text: The Australian Terrier is a small breed of dog of the terrier type.

Barbet (dog).text: The Barbet is a medium-sized breed of French water dog. It is a rare breed. The breed's name comes from the French word barbe, meaning 'beard'.

Basenji.text: The Basenji is a breed of hunting dog created from stock that originated in Central Africa, including in the Republic of the Congo and other adjacent tropical African countries.

Basset Hound.text: The Basset Hound is a short-legged breed of scent hound. The Basset Hound was developed in Great Britain from several now-extinct strains of French basset breeds.

Beagle.text: The Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound. It was bred primarily for hunting rabbit or hare, known as beagling.

Bearded Collie.text: The Bearded Collie, also called Beardie, Highland Collie, or Hairy Mountain Dog is a British breed of herding dog of the collie type.

Beauceron.text: The Beauceron is a herding dog breed originating from the plains of Central France. The Beauceron is also known as Berger de Beauce or Bas Rouge.

Bedlington Terrier.text: The Bedlington Terrier is a breed of small dog named after the mining town of Bedlington, Northumberland in North East England.

Belgian Griffon.text: The Griffon Bruxellois or Brussels Griffon is a breed of toy dog, named for their city of origin of Brussels, Belgium.

Belgian Laekenois.text: The Belgian Shepherd, also known as the Belgian Sheepdog or the Chien de Berger Belge, is a Belgian breed of herding dog of medium size.

Belgian Malinois.text: The Belgian Shepherd, also known as the Belgian Sheepdog or the Chien de Berger Belge, is a Belgian breed of herding dog of medium size.

Belgian Sheepdog.text: The Belgian Shepherd, also known as the Belgian Sheepdog or the Chien de Berger Belge, is a Belgian breed of herding dog of medium size.

Belgian Tervuren.text: The Belgian Shepherd, also known as the Belgian Sheepdog or the Chien de Berger Belge, is a Belgian breed of herding dog of medium size.

Berger Picard.text: The Berger Picard or Picardy Shepherd, is a French herding dog originating in Picardy. These dogs nearly became extinct after both World War I and World War II and remains a rare breed.

Bernedoodle.text: This is a list of common dog crossbreeds. These are crossbreed dogs created deliberately by crossing two purebred dogs.

Bernese Mountain Dog.text: The Bernese Mountain Dog, German: Berner Sennenhund or Dürrbächler, is a large dog breed originating from the canton of Bern, Switzerland and the Swiss Alps.

Bichon Frise.text: The Bichon Frisé or Bichon à Poil Frisé is a Franco-Belgian breed of small toy dog of bichon type.

Biewer Terrier.text: The Biewer Terrier is a toy dog of German descent that is the result of two Yorkshire Terriers with a recessive piebald gene breeding. It is usually kept as a companion animal or a show dog.

Black Russian Terrier.text: The Black Russian Terrier, also known as the Chornyi Terrier, is a breed of dog from the USSR.

Black and Tan Coonhound.text: The Black and Tan Coonhound is a breed of hunting dog.

Bloodhound.text: The bloodhound is a large scent hound, originally bred for hunting deer, wild boar, rabbits, and since the Middle Ages, for tracking people.

Bluetick Coonhound.text: The Bluetick Coonhound is a breed of coonhound originating in the United States. The Bluetick Coonhound is known for its friendly personality, cold nose, and deep bawl mouth.

Boerboel.text: The Boerboel is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog. It is large, with a short coat, strong bone structure and well-developed muscles.

Bolognese dog.text: The Bolognese is an Italian breed of small dog of Bichon type. It falls in the toy dog group and is commonly kept as a companion dog.

Border Collie.text: The Border Collie is a breed of British herding dog of the collie type of medium size.

Border Terrier.text: The Border Terrier is a British breed of small, rough-coated terrier.

Borzoi.text: The Borzoi or Russian Hunting Sighthound is a Russian breed of hunting dog of the sighthound type.

Boston Terrier.text: The Boston Terrier is a breed of dog originating in the United States of America. It was accepted in 1893 by the American Kennel Club as a non-sporting breed.

Bouvier Des Flandres.text: The Bouvier des Flandres is a herding dog breed originating in Flanders, Belgium.

Boxer (dog).text: The Boxer is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.

Boykin Spaniel.text: The Boykin Spaniel is a medium-sized breed of dog, a Spaniel bred for hunting wild turkeys and ducks in the Wateree River Swamp of South Carolina, in the United States.

Briard.text: The Briard or Berger de Brie is a French breed of large shepherd dog, traditionally used both for herding sheep and to defend them.

Brittany.text: Brittany is a peninsula, historical region and cultural area in the north-west of modern France, covering the western part of what was known as Armorica in Roman Gaul.

Brittany Spaniel.text: The Brittany Spaniel or Breton Spaniel is a French breed of gun dog of spaniel type, bred primarily for bird hunting. In the United States it may be called simply Brittany.

Brussels Griffon.text: The Griffon Bruxellois or Brussels Griffon is a breed of toy dog, named for their city of origin of Brussels, Belgium.

Bull Mastiff.text: The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.

Bull Terrier.text: The Bull Terrier is a breed of dog in the terrier family. There is also a miniature version of this breed, the Miniature Bull Terrier.

Bulldog.text: The Bulldog is a British breed of dog of mastiff type. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.

Bullmastiff.text: The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.

Cairn Terrier.text: The Cairn Terrier is a terrier breed originating in the Scottish Highlands and recognised as one of Scotland's earliest working dogs.

Canaan Dog.text: The Canaan Dog is a dog breed developed in the early 20th century from semiwild pariah dogs that were the descendants of animals present in the region since biblical times.

Cane Corso.text: The Cane Corso is an Italian breed of mastiff. It is usually kept as a companion dog or guard dog; it may also be used to protect livestock.

Cardigan Welsh Corgi.text: The Cardigan Welsh Corgi is one of two different varieties of livestock-herding dog breeds known as Welsh Corgis, with the other being the Pembroke Welsh Corgi.

Carolina Dog.text: The Carolina dog, also known as a yellow dog, yaller dog, American dingo, or Dixie dingo, is a breed of medium-sized dog occasionally found feral in the Southeastern United States, especially in isolated stretches of longleaf pines and cypress swamps.

Catahoula Leopard Dog.text: The Catahoula Leopard Dog is an American dog breed named after Catahoula Parish, Louisiana. It became the state dog of Louisiana in 1979.

Cavalier King Charles Spaniel.text: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel (CKCS) is a British breed of toy dog of spaniel type.

Cesky Terrier.text: The Cesky Terrier is a small terrier type dog originating in Czechoslovakia.

Chesapeake Bay Retriever.text: The Chesapeake Bay Retriever is a large breed of dog belonging to the retriever, gundog, and sporting breed groups.

Chihuahua (dog breed).text: The Chihuahua or Chihuahueño is a Mexican breed of toy dog and the smallest recognized dog breed in the world.

Chinese Crested.text: The Chinese Crested Dog is a hairless breed of dog.

Chinese Shar-Pei.text:
The Shar Pei is a dog breed from
southern China. Traditionally kept as a property guardian, the Shar Pei was driven to the brink of extinction in the 20th century.

Chinook (dog).text: The Chinook is a breed of sled dog, developed in the state of New Hampshire during the early 20th century. The Chinook is New Hampshire's official state dog.

Chow Chow.text: The Chow Chow is a spitz-type of dog breed originally from Northern China.

Cirneco dell'Etna.text: The Cirneco dell'Etna is an Italian breed of hunting dog from the Mediterranean island of Sicily. It is named for the Etna volcano in eastern Sicily.

Clumber Spaniel.text: The Clumber Spaniel is a breed of dog of the spaniel type, developed in the United Kingdom.

Cockapoo.text: The cockapoo, also known as a cockerpoo or a spoodle, is a dog crossbreed bred from the Cocker Spaniel and the Poodle, most commonly the Miniature Poodle.

Collie.text: Collies form a distinctive type of herding dogs, including many related landraces and standardized breeds. The type originated in Scotland and Northern England.

Corgi.text: The Welsh Corgi is a small type of herding dog that originated in Wales. The name corgi is thought to be derived from the Welsh words cor and ci, meaning "dwarf" and "dog", respectively.

Coton de Tulear.text: The Coton de Tuléar is a breed of small dog named for the city of Tuléar in Madagascar.

Curly-Coated Retriever.text: The Curly-coated Retriever is a breed of dog originally bred in England for upland bird and waterfowl hunting.

Dachshund.text: The Dachshund, also known as the Dackel or Teckel, is a German breed of short-legged, long-bodied dog of hound type. It may be smooth-haired, wire-haired, or long-haired, in various colors.

Dalmatian dog.text: The Dalmatian is a breed of dog with a white coat marked with dark-coloured spots.

Dandie Dinmont Terrier.text: A Dandie Dinmont Terrier is a small Scottish dog breed in the terrier family. The breed has a very long body, short legs, and a distinctive topknot of hair on the head.

Dobermann.text: The Dobermann is a German breed of medium-large working dog of pinscher type. In Canada and the United States it is known as the Doberman Pinscher.

Dogo Argentino.text: The Dogo Argentino is an Argentine breed of large dog of mastiff type.

Dogue de Bordeaux.text: The Dogue de Bordeaux, also known as the Bordeaux Mastiff, French Mastiff or Bordeauxdog, is a large French mastiff breed.

Dutch Shepherd.text: The Dutch Shepherd is a herding dog of Dutch origin.

English Cocker Spaniel.text: The English Cocker Spaniel is a breed of gun dog. It is noteworthy for producing one of the most varied numbers of pups in a litter among all dog breeds.

English Foxhound.text: The English Foxhound is one of the four foxhound breeds of dog. It is a cousin of the American Foxhound. They are scent hounds, bred to hunt foxes by scent.

English Mastiff.text: The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large dog of mastiff type.

English Setter.text: The English Setter is a medium-size breed of dog. It is part of the setter group, which includes the red Irish Setters, Irish Red and White Setters, and black-and-tan Gordon Setters.

English Springer Spaniel.text: The English Springer Spaniel is a breed of gun dog in the Spaniel group traditionally used for flushing and retrieving game.

English Toy Spaniel.text: The King Charles Spaniel is a small dog breed of the spaniel type. In 1903, The Kennel Club combined four separate toy spaniel breeds under this single title.

Entlebucher Mountain Dog.text: The Entlebucher Sennenhund or Entlebucher Mountain Dog is a medium-sized herding dog, it is the smallest of the four regional breeds that constitute the Sennenhund dog type.

Estrela Mountain Dog.text: The Estrela Mountain Dog or Cão da Serra da Estrela is a Portuguese breed of large flock guardian dog indigenous to the Serra da Estrela mountain range in central Portugal.

Eurasier.text: The Eurasier, or Eurasian, is a spitz type breed of dog that originated in Germany through cross-breeding between popular European and Asian Spitz.

Feist (dog).text: A feist is a small hunting dog. This group descended from the terriers brought over to the United States by British miners and other immigrants.

Field Spaniel.text: The Field Spaniel is a medium-sized dog breed of spaniel type.

Finnish Lapphund.text: The Finnish Lapphund is a hardy, easy-going, medium-size breed of Spitz type. Traditionally it has been used for herding reindeer.

Finnish Spitz.text: The Finnish Spitz is a breed of dog originating in Finland. The breed was originally trained to hunt all types of game from squirrels and other rodents to bears.

Flat-Coated Retriever.text: The Flat-coated Retriever is a gun dog breed originating from England. It was developed as a retriever both on land and in the water.

Formosan Mountain Dog.text: The Taiwan Dog is a breed of small or medium dog indigenous to Taiwan. These dogs are also known as the Formosan Mountain Dog.

French Bulldog.text: The French Bulldog is a French breed of companion dog or toy dog.

French Poodle.text: The Poodle, called the Pudel in German and the Caniche in French, is a breed of water dog.

French Spaniel.text: The French Spaniel is a breed of dog of the Spaniel-like setter. It was developed in France and Canada as a hunting dog, descended from dogs of the 14th century.

German Longhaired Pointer.text: The German Longhaired Pointer or Deutsch Langhaar is a German breed of gundog of pointer type.

German Pinscher.text: The German Pinscher or Deutscher Pinscher is a German breed of dog in the Pinscher and Schnauzer group.

German Shepherd.text: The German Shepherd, also known in Britain as an Alsatian, is a German breed of working dog of medium to large size. It is characterized by its intelligent and obedient nature.

German Shorthaired Pointer.text: The German Shorthaired Pointer or Deutsch Kurzhaar is a German breed of continental pointing dog of Braque type. It originated in the nineteenth century in what is now Germany.

German Spitz.text: The German Spitz is a breed of spitz-type dogs from Germany.

German Wirehaired Pointer.text: The German Wirehaired Pointer or Deutsch Drahthaar is a German breed of pointing dog of Griffon type.

Giant Schnauzer.text: The Giant Schnauzer or Riesenschnauzer is a German breed of dog of Schnauzer type. It is larger than the other two Schnauzer breeds, the Standard Schnauzer and the Miniature Schnauzer.

Glen of Imaal Terrier.text: The Glen of Imaal Terrier is a rare Irish dog breed from County Wicklow, Ireland, and one of four original Irish terrier breeds native to Ireland.

Golden Retriever.text: The Golden Retriever is a Scottish breed of retriever dog of medium-large size. It is characterised by a gentle and affectionate nature and a striking golden coat.

Goldendoodle.text: The Goldendoodle is a designer dog created by crossbreeding a Golden Retriever and a Poodle.

Gordon Setter.text: The Gordon Setter is a Scottish large breed of dog, a member of the setter family that also includes both the better-known Irish Setter and the English Setter.

Grand Basset Griffon Vendeen.text: The Grand Basset Griffon Vendéen or GBGV is a dog breed from France.

Great Dane.text: The Great Dane is a German breed of large mastiff-sighthound, which descends from hunting dogs of the Middle Ages used to hunt bears, wild boar, and deer.

Great Pyrenees.text: The Pyrenean Mountain Dog is a French breed of livestock guardian dog. In France, it is commonly called the Patou. It is known as the Great Pyrenees in the US.

Greater Swiss Mountain Dog.text: The Greater Swiss Mountain Dog is a dog breed which was developed in the Swiss Alps. The name Sennenhund refers to people called Senn or Senner, dairymen and herders in the Swiss Alps.

Greek Shepherd.text: The Greek Shepherd or Greek Sheepdog is a breed of livestock guardian dog from Greece.

Greyhound.text: The Greyhound is a breed of dog and a sighthound.

Harrier (dog).text:
The Harrier is a medium-sized dog breed of the hound class, 
used for hunting hares by trailing them.

Havanese dog.text: The Havanese, a bichon-type dog, is the national dog of Cuba, developed from the now extinct Blanquito de la Habana. The Blanquito descended from the also now-extinct Bichón Tenerife.

Hound.text: A hound is a type of hunting dog used by hunters to track or chase prey.

Ibizan Hound.text: The Ibizan Hound is a lean, agile dog of the hound family. There are two hair types of the breed: smooth and wire. The more commonly seen type is the smooth.

Icelandic Sheepdog.text: The Icelandic Sheepdog, is an Icelandic breed of dog of Nordic Spitz type.

Irish Red and White Setter.text: The Irish Red and White Setter is a breed of dog. As with all setters, it is classified as a gundog in the UK and is included in the sporting group in America and Canada.

Irish Setter.text: The Irish Setter is a setter, a breed of gundog, and family dog originating in Ireland.

Irish Terrier.text: The Irish Terrier is a dog breed from Ireland, one of many breeds of terrier. The Irish Terrier is considered one of the oldest terrier breeds.

Irish Wolfhound.text: The Irish Wolfhound is a breed of large sighthound that has, by its presence and substantial size, inspired literature, poetry and mythology.

Italian Greyhound.text: The Italian Greyhound or Piccolo Levriero Italiano is an Italian breed of small sighthound. It was bred to hunt hare and rabbit, but is kept mostly as a companion dog.

Jack Russell Terrier.text: The Jack Russell Terrier is a British breed of small terrier. It is principally white-bodied and may have a smooth, rough, or broken coat, with markings of various colours.

Jagdterrier.text: The Jagdterrier is a type of working terrier, originating in Germany, that is used for hunting quarry both above and underground. This breed of terrier is also called the German Hunt Terrier.

Japanese Chin.text: The Japanese Chin, also known as the Japanese Spaniel, is a toy dog breed, being both a lap dog and a companion dog, with a distinctive heritage.

Japanese Spitz.text: The Japanese Spitz  is a Japanese small to medium breed of dog of the Spitz type.

Kai Ken.text: The Kai Ken  is a breed of dog native to the Kai region, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan, where it is a national monument.

Karelian Bear Dog.text: The Karelian Bear Dog is a Finnish breed of dog. In its home country, it is seen by many as a national treasure. Karelian Bear Dogs will hunt a variety of animals.

Keeshond.text: The Keeshond is a medium-sized dog with a plush, two-layer coat of silver and black fur with a ruff and a curled tail.

Kerry Blue Terrier.text: The Kerry Blue Terrier or Irish Blue Terrier is an Irish breed of dog of terrier type.

Kishu Ken.text: The Kishu  is a Japanese breed of dog. It is descended from ancient medium-sized breeds and named after the Kishu region, now Mie Prefecture and Wakayama Prefecture.

Kooikerhondje.text: The Kooikerhondje is a small spaniel-type dog breed of Dutch ancestry that was originally used as a working dog, particularly in a decoy to lure ducks.

Korean Jindo.text: The Jindo dog is an indigenous dog native to the island of Jindo in South Korea. It is also known as Jindo-gyeon and formerly known as the Chindo dog.

Kromfohrlander.text: The Kromfohrländer is a modern German breed of companion dog. It originated in Germany in the years after the end of the Second World War.

Kuvasz.text: The Kuvasz is a Hungarian breed of flock guardian dog. Mention of the breed can be found in old Hungarian texts.

Labradoodle.text: A labradoodle is a crossbreed dog created by crossing a Labrador Retriever and a Standard or Miniature Poodle.

Labrador Retriever.text: The Labrador Retriever, also known simply as the Labrador or Lab, is a British breed of retriever gun dog.

Lagotto Romagnolo.text: The Lagotto Romagnolo is an Italian breed of dog.

Lakeland Terrier.text: The Lakeland Terrier is a dog breed, which takes its name from its place of origin, the Lake District in England. The dog is a small to mid-size member of the Terrier family.

Lancashire Heeler.text: The Lancashire Heeler is a small breed of dog developed for use as a drover and herder of cattle. The Lancashire Heeler is listed by the Kennel Club (UK) as an endangered breed.

Leonberger.text: The Leonberger is a German breed of large dog. The breed name derives from that of the city of Leonberg, in Baden-Württemberg, where it was bred in the mid-nineteenth century.

Lhasa Apso.text: The Lhasa Apso is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet. Traditionally the breed has been used as an interior watchdog.

Lowchen.text: The Löwchen or Little Lion Dog is a breed of small dog. The Löwchen once had the dubious distinction, like the Portuguese Water Dog and the Havanese, of being the rarest dog in the world.

Maltese dog.text: Maltese dog refers both to an ancient variety of dwarf, white-coated dog breed from Italy and generally associated also with the island of Malta, and to a modern breed of similar dogs in the toy group, genetically related to the Bichon, Bolognese, and Havanese breeds.

Manchester Terrier.text: The Manchester Terrier is a breed of dog of the smooth-haired terrier type. It was first bred in the 19th century to control vermin, notably rats, at which it excelled.

Mastiff.text: A mastiff is a large and powerful type of dog.

Miniature American Shepherd.text: The Miniature American Shepherd, frequently abbreviated MAS, is a small herding dog breed. The MAS is highly intelligent and biddable.

Miniature Bull Terrier.text: The Miniature Bull Terrier is a breed with origins in the extinct English White Terrier, the Dalmatian and the Bulldog.

Miniature Fox Terrier.text: The Miniature Fox Terrier is a small, fine, lightweight working terrier developed as a hunting dog and vermin router. It is known colloquially in its native Australia as the “Mini Foxie”.

Miniature Pinscher.text: The Miniature Pinscher or Zwergpinscher is a German breed of small dog of Pinscher type.

Miniature Schnauzer.text: The Miniature Schnauzer is a German breed of small dog of Schnauzer type. It originated in Germany in the late nineteenth century.

Mudi.text: The Mudi is a herding dog breed from Hungary. It is closely related to the Puli and Pumi, from which it was separated in the 1930s.

Neapolitan Mastiff.text: The Neapolitan Mastiff or Mastino Napoletano is an Italian breed of large dog of mastiff type.

Newfoundland.text: Newfoundland and Labrador is the easternmost province of Canada, in the country's Atlantic region.

Norfolk Terrier.text: The Norfolk Terrier is a British breed of dog.

Norwegian Buhund.text: The Norwegian Buhund is a breed of dog of the spitz type. It is closely related to the Icelandic Sheepdog and the Jämthund.

Norwegian Elkhound.text: The Norwegian Elkhound is one of the Northern Spitz-type breeds of dog and is the National Dog of Norway. The Elkhound has served as a hunter, guardian, herder, and defender.

Norwich Terrier.text: The Norwich Terrier is a breed of dog originating in England, and was bred to hunt small rodents. One of the smallest terriers, these dogs are relatively rare.

Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever.text: The Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever is a medium-sized gun dog bred primarily for hunting. It is often referred to as a "toller".

Old English Sheepdog.text: The Old English Sheepdog is a large breed of dog that emerged in England from early types of herding dog. Other names for the breed include Shepherd's Dog and bob-tailed sheep-dog.

Olde English Bulldogge.text: The Olde English Bulldogge is an American dog breed, recognized by the United Kennel Club (UKC) in January 2014. The breed is listed in the UKC Guardian Dog Group.

Otterhound.text: The Otterhound is an English dog breed. It is a scent hound and is currently recognised by the Kennel Club as a Vulnerable Native Breed with around 600 animals worldwide.

Papillon dog.text: The Épagneul Nain Continental or Continental Toy Spaniel is a Belgian and French breed of dog of spaniel type and of miniature or toy size.

Parson Russell Terrier.text: The Parson Russell Terrier is an English breed of small white terrier that was the original Fox Terrier of the 18th century.

Patterdale Terrier.text: The Patterdale Terrier is a breed of dog descended from the Northern terrier breeds of the early 18th century, originally bred in Patterdale in the Lake District.

Pekingese.text: The Pekingese is a breed of toy dog, originating in China.

Pembroke Welsh Corgi.text: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi is a cattle herding dog breed that originated in Pembrokeshire, Wales.

Perro de Presa Canario.text: The Presa Canario is a Spanish breed of large dog of mastiff or catch dog type.

Peruvian Inca Orchid.text: The Peruvian Hairless Dog or Perro Sin Pelo del Perú is a Peruvian breed of hairless dog. It is the only living breed of dog indigenous to Peru.

Petit Basset Griffon Vendeen.text: The Petit Basset Griffon Vendéen is a French breed of small dog of scent hound type, bred to trail hares in bramble-filled terrain of the Vendée district of France.

Pharaoh Hound.text: The Pharaoh Hound or Kelb tal-Fenek is a Maltese breed of warren hound. It is traditionally used for rabbit-hunting in the rocky terrain of the islands; the Maltese name means "rabbit dog".

Pit bull.text: Pit bull is an umbrella term for several types of dog believed to have descended from bull and terriers.

Plott Hound.text: The Plott Hound, often referred to as the Plott, is a large scent hound, originally bred for hunting bears.

Pointer (dog breed).text: The Pointer, sometimes called the English Pointer, is a medium-sized breed of pointing dog developed in England.

Polish Lowland Sheepdog.text: The Polish Lowland Sheepdog, is a medium-sized, shaggy-coated, sheep dog breed native to Poland.

Pomeranian dog.text: The Pomeranian is a breed of dog of the Spitz type that is named for the Pomerania region in north-west Poland and north-east Germany in Central Europe.

Poodle.text: The Poodle, called the Pudel in German and the Caniche in French, is a breed of water dog.

Portuguese Podengo Pequeno.text: The Portuguese Podengo, also known as the Podengo Português or Portuguese Warren Hound, is a Portuguese breed of dog of warren hound type.

Portuguese Pointer.text: The Portuguese Pointing Dog or Perdigueiro Português is a Portuguese breed of pointer dog. It is one of several Portuguese pointing breeds and is mainly used in hunting red-legged partridge.

Portuguese Sheepdog.text: The Portuguese Sheepdog is a medium-sized breed of dog of the herding dog type, and is one of the indigenous regional dogs of Portugal.

Portuguese Water Dog.text: The Portuguese Water Dog, also known as the Algarvian Water Dog, or Portuguese Fishing Dog, is a breed of dog that originated from the Algarve region of Portugal.

Presa Canario.text: The Presa Canario is a Spanish breed of large dog of mastiff or catch dog type.

Pug.text: The Pug is a breed of dog with the physically distinctive features of a wrinkly, short-muzzled face, and curled tail.

Puggle.text: A puggle is a dog crossbred from a pug and a beagle. The breed originated in the 1990s in the United States.

Puli dog.text: The Puli is a small-medium breed of Hungarian herding dog known for its long, corded coat. The tight curls of the coat appear similar to dreadlocks.

Pumi dog.text: The Pumi is a medium-small breed of sheep dog from Hungary. They are capable herding dogs, able to gather and work close to farm stock, particularly sheep, to keep them under control.

Pyrenean Mastiff.text: The Pyrenean Mastiff or Mastín del Pirineo is a Spanish breed of large livestock guardian dog from the autonomous community of Aragón in north-eastern Spain.

Pyrenean Shepherd.text: The Pyrenean Sheepdog, the Chien de Berger des Pyrénées in French, is a small to medium-sized breed of herding dog from the Pyrenees Mountains region of France.

Rat Terrier.text: The Rat Terrier is an American dog breed with a background as a farm dog and hunting companion. They share much ancestry with the small hunting dogs known as feists.

Redbone Coonhound.text: The Redbone Coonhound is an American breed of hunting dog.

Rhodesian Ridgeback.text: The Rhodesian Ridgeback is a large dog breed originally bred in Southern Africa. The original breed standard was drafted by F.R.

Rottweiler.text: The Rottweiler is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.

Russian Toy.text: The Russian Toy is a very small breed of dog originally bred in Russia from the English Toy Terrier. There are two types of coats in the breed: smooth coat and long coat.

Saluki.text: The Saluki or Arabian hound or Persian hound is a standardised breed developed from sighthounds – dogs that hunt primarily by sight rather than strong scent – that was once used by nomadic tribes to run down game animals.

Samoyed dog.text: The Samoyed is a breed of herding dog with a thick, white, double-layered coat. They are spitz-type dogs which take their name from the Samoyedic peoples.

Schipperke.text: A Schipperke is a small breed of dog that is believed to have originated in the 1600s in Flanders. In their home country of Belgium they are considered a small shepherd.

Schnauzer.text: The Schnauzer is a dog breed type that originated in Germany in the 14th to 16th centuries.

Scottish Terrier.text: The Scottish Terrier, popularly called the Scottie, is a breed of dog.

Sealyham Terrier.text: The Sealyham Terrier is a rare Welsh breed of small to medium-sized terrier that originated in Wales as a working dog.

Shetland Sheepdog.text: The Shetland Sheepdog, also known as the Sheltie, is a breed of herding dog that originated in the Shetland Islands of Scotland. It was formally recognized by the Kennel Club in 1909.

Shiba Inu.text: The Shiba Inu  is a breed of hunting dog from Japan. A small-to-medium breed, it is the smallest of the six original dog breeds native to Japan. The Shiba Inu was originally bred for hunting.

Shih Tzu.text: The Shih Tzu is a toy dog or pet dog breed originating from Tibet and believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso.

Siberian Husky.text: The Siberian Husky is a breed of medium-sized working sled dog. The breed belongs to the Spitz genetic family.

Silky Terrier.text: The Australian Silky Terrier or simply Silky Terrier is a small breed of dog of the terrier dog type.

Skye Terrier.text: The Skye Terrier is a Scottish breed of terrier. It is long, low, hardy and short-legged, and in the twenty-first century is among the most endangered breeds of the United Kingdom.

Small M\u00fcnsterl\u00e4nder.text: The Small Münsterländer is a versatile hunting-pointing-retrieving dog breed that reached its current form in the area around Münster, Germany.

Smooth Fox Terrier.text: The Smooth Fox Terrier is a breed of dog, one of many terrier breeds. It was the first breed in the Fox Terrier family to be given official recognition by The Kennel Club.

Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier.text: The soft-coated Wheaten Terrier is a pure-breed terrier originating from Ireland. Wheatens typically have one of two coat types: Irish or Heavy (American).

Soft-Coated Wheaten Terrier.text: The soft-coated Wheaten Terrier is a pure-breed terrier originating from Ireland. Wheatens typically have one of two coat types: Irish or Heavy (American).

Spanish Water Dog.text: The Spanish Water Dog or Perro de Agua Español is a Spanish breed of water dog.

Spinone Italiano.text: The Spinone Italiano is an Italian breed of hunting dog, traditionally used for tracking, for pointing and for retrieving game.

St. Bernard (dog).text: The St. Bernard or Saint Bernard is a breed of very large working dog from the Western Alps; they were originally bred for rescue work by the hospice of the Great St Bernard Pass on the Italian-Swiss border, with Switzerland recognized as its country of origin by the FCI.

Stabyhoun.text: The Stabyhoun, or Stabijhoun or Stabij, is one of the rarest dog breeds in the world.

Staffordshire Bull Terrier.text: The Staffordshire Bull Terrier, also called the Staffy or Stafford, is a purebred dog of small to medium size in the terrier group that originated in the northern parts of Birmingham and in Staffordshire, for which it is named.

Standard Schnauzer.text: The Standard Schnauzer or Mittelschnauzer is a German breed of dog in the Pinscher and Schnauzer group.

Sussex Spaniel.text: The Sussex Spaniel is a breed of dog native to Sussex, in southern England. It is a low, compact spaniel and is similar in appearance to the Clumber Spaniel.

Swedish Vallhund.text: The Swedish Vallhund, also known as the Västgötaspets and Swedish cow dog, is a breed of dog native to Sweden.

Terrier.text: Terrier is a type of dog originally bred to hunt vermin. A terrier is a dog of any one of many breeds or landraces of the terrier type, which are typically small, wiry, game, and fearless.

Thai Ridgeback.text: The Thai Ridgeback is a dog breed from Thailand.

Tibetan Mastiff.text: The Tibetan Mastiff is a large Tibetan dog breed.

Tibetan Spaniel.text: The Tibetan Spaniel is a breed of assertive, small dogs originating in Tibet.

Tibetan Terrier.text: The Tibetan Terrier is a medium-sized breed of dog that originated in Tibet. Despite its name, it is not a member of the terrier group.

Tosa (dog).text: The Tosa, also known as the Japanese Mastiff, is a dog breed of Japanese origin that is considered rare.

Toy Fox Terrier.text: The Toy Fox Terrier is a small terrier breed of dog, directly descended from the larger Smooth Fox Terrier but since 1936, it has been registered in the United States with the UKC as a separate breed.

Treeing Tennessee Brindle.text: The Treeing Tennessee Brindle is a breed of cur. Since 1995, its records have been maintained through the American Kennel Club's Foundation Stock Service Program.

Treeing Walker Coonhound.text: The Treeing Walker Coonhound is a breed of hound descended primarily from English and American Foxhounds.

Vizsla.text: The Vizsla, also known as Hungarian Vizsla, Magyar Vizsla or Hungarian Pointer, is a dog breed from Hungary and belongs to the Fédération Cynologique Internationale (FCI) group 7, the Canadian Kennel Club (CKC) group 1, and the American Kennel Club.

Weimaraner.text: The Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.

Welsh Springer Spaniel.text: The Welsh Springer Spaniel is a breed of dog and a member of the spaniel family.

Welsh Terrier.text: The Welsh Terrier also known as the Welshie, is believed to have originated in the 1700s in Wales and was originally bred for hunting fox, rodents and badger; in the remote mountains of northern Wales, but during the last century, it has mainly been bred for showing.

West Highland White Terrier.text: The West Highland White Terrier is a Scottish dog breed with a distinctive white harsh coat and somewhat soft white undercoat.

Whippet.text: The Whippet is a British breed of sighthound. It closely resembles the Greyhound and the smaller Italian Greyhound, and is intermediate between them in size.

Wire Fox Terrier.text: The Wire Fox Terrier is a breed of dog, one of many terrier breeds.

Wirehaired Pointing Griffon.text: The Wirehaired Pointing Griffon is a breed of dog used in hunting as a gundog.

Wirehaired Vizsla.text: The Hungarian Wirehaired Vizsla or Hungarian Wirehaired Pointer is a Hungarian breed of pointer dog.

Xoloitzcuintli.text: The Xoloitzcuintle is one of several breeds of hairless dog. It is found in standard, intermediate, and miniature sizes.

Yorkshire Terrier.text: The Yorkshire Terrier, also known as a Yorkie, is a British breed of toy dog of terrier type.
